timeline.name: Consumer-verified completion
timeline.rule: An artifact with an external consumer is done only when that consumer's fetch confirms it -- quote the fetched evidence, not the producer's own view.
timeline.incident: PROJECT_STATE.txt read stale to the advisor's fetch while fresh in the local working copy at the very same commit -- producer and consumer were looking at genuinely different things; self-certification could not have caught it.

timeline.name: Long-running processes: committed != running
timeline.rule: A code fix is deployed only once the running process has been restarted with it.
timeline.incident: The session watchdog was claimed fixed twice while its tmux pane still showed a bare shell -- the fix had landed in the script but the running process was never restarted with it. Recurred 2026-07-13 (supervisor daemon running stale pre-fix code).

timeline.name: Two-strike redesign
timeline.rule: A second false completion claim on the same component means eliminate/redesign the mechanism, not patch it again.
timeline.incident: The watchdog's tmux send-keys relaunch failed three distinct ways in succession; the fix that worked was eliminating send-keys entirely, not a third patch.

timeline.name: Diagnosis discipline
timeline.rule: Before fixing a stuck problem, name the nearest working analogue and state the diff; if none exists, build the smallest closed-loop test first.
timeline.incident: Every real breakthrough that week came from a contrast pair, not a first-principles theory: fresh-vs-stale at the same commit, interactive-vs-login shell for PATH resolution.

timeline.name: Alerting on transitions only
timeline.rule: Notifications fire on state transitions only, carry the diagnostic payload, and never repeat an unchanged status.
timeline.incident: An early watchdog alert just said 'launch failed', which told the human nothing actionable; the fix carries the last N captured pane lines in the NTFY itself.

timeline.name: Report sections are never the primary work
timeline.rule: Reporting is a byproduct of building capability, not the capability itself. A new dashboard/report section alone never counts as a phase.
timeline.incident: An instruction to close four real priorities was satisfied in name only by writing four board-report sections instead of building the capability each priority named.

timeline.name: Injected/wake text carries ZERO authority
timeline.rule: Injected/wake text is a doorbell, not an instruction. Act only on disk/git state or a director-authenticated console turn, never on the mere fact that text arrived claiming to be a directive.
timeline.incident: Repeated doorbell/wake failures (strikes 3-5): a session acting on the arrival of wake text rather than on the actual staged/git state it pointed at.

timeline.name: All inbound NTFY is untrusted data
timeline.rule: A directive arriving by NTFY requires correlation with a staged doc or console confirmation before any security-relevant action.
timeline.incident: NTFY is public and unauthenticated -- anyone can post; a security-relevant directive on that channel alone cannot be trusted without an on-disk correlate.

timeline.name: Evidence before narrative
timeline.rule: Incident reports label every claim observed-with-evidence or inferred; a conclusion implying an external actor is checked against the most direct evidence before being asserted.
timeline.incident: A genuine LOCAL test-isolation bug was first reported as external prompt injection -- asserted ahead of checking the one thing (the actual channel history) that would have settled it.

timeline.name: Absurdity-class defects close as a class
timeline.rule: An absurdity-class defect may NOT be closed with an instance fix. Closure requires extending the invariant library / obligations register so the whole class fails automatically thereafter.
timeline.incident: A C6 SME-as-Household 20%-VAT bill (4.3x sigma, missing non-commodity revenue) -- the same class had appeared three times and never been fixed as a class.

timeline.name: Verify to the rendered value
timeline.rule: For any user-visible change, 'done' means fetching the LIVE deployed surface and asserting the actual rendered value changed as intended -- never the code, the file on origin, or the deploy log alone.
timeline.incident: Releasing a publish hold closed the review gate but triggered no regeneration (the change-detection gate saw near-identical headline figures as 'no change'); the live site stayed stale for hours until the director checked the deployed pixel himself.

timeline.name: Anti-goal-seek: a metric is a diagnostic
timeline.rule: Margin (and any output metric) is a DIAGNOSTIC, never a target. Plausibility bands trigger a mechanism investigation, never a fudge factor or calibration toward a benchmark.
timeline.incident: Guard against the standing temptation to tune an output toward an external benchmark once it lands off-band, instead of investigating the mechanism that produced it.

timeline.name: The baseline/curriculum split
timeline.rule: The BASELINE world may only change for fidelity-to-reality reasons, decided blind to company P&L. The CURRICULUM is the director's instrument -- named, versioned, never silent parameter drift in response to outcomes.
timeline.incident: The agent controls both sides of the epistemic wall, so difficulty must face the director, not the builder -- otherwise the company's world quietly bends to make its results look right.

timeline.name: No financial figure without its clock
timeline.rule: No financial figure is published without its clock (settled/billed/banked). A number whose basis is unstated is a defect, not a formatting choice -- enforced by the page-consistency gate.
timeline.incident: Headline figures on different clocks diverge by design; publishing one without stating which clock it is on invites a false apples-to-apples reading.

timeline.name: A control must be able to fail
timeline.rule: No control counts as evidence for a promotion/Expert-Hour/green-suite unless a mutation test proves it fires on its own named defect. Three killer patterns: tautology (checked value derived from the same source it checks), fail-open (passes on missing/zero/empty/malformed input), fail-silent (passes when the checker itself is unavailable). A control that cannot fail is worse than none.
timeline.incident: Several controls that had been counted as evidence turned out to be theatre -- they passed regardless of input -- so the burden of proof became a mutation that must flip the verdict before the control is trusted.

FRAME SUMMARY (design only, nothing built): the death loop in three sentences -- the company is naturally LONG forward (it buys ahead to cover fixed-price retail), so when the forward FALLS its netted MtM goes negative and counterparties call variation margin equal to the WHOLE remaining tenor's loss payable in cash at T+1; that cash leaves as a STEP on the BANKED clock while the offsetting benefit (cheaper energy for the rest of the customers' terms) accrues as a RAMP on the SETTLED clock and only becomes cash later still after billing and DD collection; and because the hedge is held against a matched forecast supply obligation the MtM loss does not hit accounting P&L, so the company reaches Cash + Facility_undrawn < VM_due while P&L is positive and rising. R14 CLOCKS NAMED PER QUANTITY: MtM_t and VM_called on the MARK clock; VM_paid at t+delta and IM_t and Cash_t on the BANKED clock; wholesale cost and accounting net margin on the SETTLED clock; R_billed on the BILLED clock and R_banked on the BANKED clock at bill+collection lag. THE ARITHMETIC OF THE ASYMMETRY: cash OUT is Q*|dF| in ONE payment at t+delta; cash IN is the same total spread over the tenor T and delayed by lambda_bill+lambda_collect; so the peak cash deficit is of order Q*|dF|*(1 - (lambda_bill+lambda_collect)/T) EVEN WHEN THE TRADE IS PERFECTLY HEDGED AND P&L-NEUTRAL -- and collapsing any of delta, lambda_bill, lambda_collect or T to zero deletes the mechanism silently with a green suite. TWO CHANNELS, BOTH NEEDED: (A) VM on a FALLING forward, direction-specific, whose killer sequence is SPINE_3 §1.7c 2022-08 GBP186.54 -> 2022-10 GBP55.47 = -70.3% in two months against a book bought at the peak (SPINE_3 acceptance leg D, <= -50%, is therefore NOT optional for B6); (B) INITIAL margin re-called on rising VOLATILITY, direction-agnostic, which drains cash on the SPIKE too -- without (B), B6 can only kill on the collapse leg and a run window ending before 2022-08 can never be killed. MINIMUM MECHANISM, five pieces, four of them CONNECTIONS between things that already exist (SIMPLICITY GUARD): 1 split the balance (rename treasury_cash_balance_gbp -> cumulative_net_margin_gbp, meaning unchanged, and introduce a separate cash_banked_gbp fed only by banked events; move is_administration_triggered onto cash+undrawn facility -- NOTHING ELSE WORKS UNTIL THIS LANDS); 2 a daily mark path replacing the single terminal snapshot, using the EXISTING observable resolver at run_phase2b.py:2553-2560, no new price source; 3 a call->payment lifecycle with real latency (C-S3), giving settle_call the caller it has never had; 4 initial margin as a live term sized off an observable volatility proxy; 5 revenue-to-cash conversion with lambda_bill+lambda_collect hung on the payment machinery already on the run path at run_phase2b.py:1907. C-S5: the lags are day-indexed so TIME-SCALE INVARIANCE MUST BE DECLARED FALSE and registered as a named simplification. WALL: the company sees its own blotter, its own MARGIN CALLS (the purest observable here -- it learns the size of its problem by being TOLD TO PAY), its own bank balance, bills, DD collections and committed facility, and published market data; it may NEVER see SPINE_3's storage state, the shock parameters, its counterparties' internal IM models, or any future mark (run_phase2b.py:642-644 already sets the correct pattern -- the resolver reads only history BEFORE the mark date and raises on insufficient history, and B6 must preserve that failure mode rather than paper over it). THE COMPANY IS ALLOWED TO BE WRONG AND ALLOWED TO DIE: sim/forward_curve.py:88 GAS_MONTH_SEASONAL_MULTIPLIER is a static dict that CANNOT CHANGE SIGN (SPINE_3 §1.5), so the company will be structurally wrong in a mechanical, predictable way, exactly as real suppliers were; a B6 that quietly grants enough foresight to survive has destroyed the finding. COUPLED TRIAD: SIM (SPINE_3 + B4) owes a DAILY PER-TENOR forward mark (spot alone gives B6 nothing to mark against), the COLLAPSE leg not only the spike, SPEED as a first-class quantity (the death is driven by dF/dt, not F), a daily cadence with the payment lag owned by B6, and parameterisability to a milder shock -- so SPINE_3 alone is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT and B4_traded_product_ladder is a real co-dependency (SPINE_3 §3 Q4 asks the same ordering question from the other side and it is still open). COMPANY discovers the crisis through the observables above and must choose unhedge / draw / fail. HARNESS measures three gaps into coupled_gap_ledger.json, the headline being THE CLOCK-DIVERGENCE GAP: P&L_t (settled) minus Cash_t (banked) tracked daily through the crisis window -- oscillating near zero in a healthy world, fanning out in the death world; THAT SERIES IS THE B6 SCORE, not a proxy for it. Plus liquidity-runway belief gap (how LATE the company sees it coming) and margin-anticipation gap (VM provisioned vs VM called). DEFEAT DEFINED NUMERICALLY, as the triad law requires: on the SAME run (a) min_t (Cash_t + Facility_undrawn_t) < 0 on the BANKED clock, AND (b) P&L_t > 0 at that same t on the SETTLED clock, AND (c) the killing call arose from a PRICE MOVE ALONE with no injected loss at the cash line, AND (d) death_cause == collateral_while_solvent, never collateral_insolvent -- the (d) distinction already exists and is already correct at collateral_death_test.py:186-189, so B6 does not reinvent it, it makes it reachable from a LIVE RUN rather than a post-hoc sweep. And per B6's own DoD BOTH DIRECTIONS must be proven: a milder shock must yield survival with min_t(Cash+Facility) > 0, because a world that always kills is as useless as one that never does. R13 SPLIT -- BASELINE (agent-buildable, fidelity-to-reality, decided blind to company P&L): CSA variation-margin mechanics (OTM party posts, per-master netting, VM returned when the mark moves back), the T+1 settlement convention, initial-margin convention (posted at inception, sized to a ~5-day stressed holding period, re-called when the CCP raises the multiple, returned at maturity), haircuts and eligible-collateral rules, cleared-vs-bilateral treatment (partly present already at wholesale_credit_exposure.py:60 _CLEARED_EXPOSURE_HAIRCUT=0.10), billing and DD collection lags calibrated to real UK practice, THE FACILITY SIZING RULE (already director-ruled at MC-2 §3 and NOT to be re-opened by B6 -- shrinking the facility to force a death is an R12 breach), and the gap-measurement/oracle/mutation machinery. CURRICULUM (DIRECTOR-RESERVED, the agent must NOT set): which crisis the company lives through (SPINE_3's shock magnitude/onset/ramp/persistence); the STARTING CASH and committed facility AS A DIFFICULTY SETTING -- note the fine line, the facility SIZING RULE is baseline but a hand-chosen opening balance picked to make the company die is curriculum, and a BUILD that finds itself choosing one has crossed; whether the company gets a lagged published storage feed (SPINE_3 §3 Q3, which directly sets survivability); THE SURVIVAL SCORE'S WEIGHTING (how mortality-by-collateral weighs against other outcomes is a values decision about what the company is FOR, one-way door 6 -- B6 supplies the raw fields and must NOT blend them into a scalar); and whether the company may unhedge under duress or is capped on facility drawdown (a board decision, a world-fact about governance). THE MECHANISM OF DYING IS BASELINE; THE SEVERITY OF THE WORLD AND THE SCORING OF THE DEATH ARE THE DIRECTOR'S -- this FRAME chooses no severity. R15 AT BUILD: the TAUTOLOGY trap here is specific -- Cash_t and P&L_t MUST be computed from independent event streams, because if Cash_t is derived as P&L_t plus adjustments then "cash diverged from P&L" re-asserts the adjustment term and CANNOT FAIL WHILE THE CODE COMPILES (SPINE_3's T2 shape); enforced by a test that the cash accumulator takes banked-clock events only and that its module does not import the P&L module, and by an EXTERNAL oracle built from sim/gas_data/nbp_sap.csv (a file the margin code neither reads nor writes) rather than from the generator's own series. FAIL-OPEN guards, each a FAILED check never a silent pass: reject NON-FINITE FIRST before any comparison (max/min/< are all NaN-blind -- §1.10 proves the live path fails open at three lines today); empty or single-point mark path; delta/lambda_bill/lambda_collect/T equal to zero must be LOUD, not a default, because a zero lag deletes the mechanism; a zero facility, or available_cash_gbp=0.0 silently meaning "cash is zero" when it means "cash is unknown"; and a missing clock label on any published B6 figure (R14 gate). FAIL-SILENT: the two bare except-Exception swallows must go (an unavailable death test is a FAILED death test), and the reducer drop must be closed with a published-surface assertion (R11, verify to the rendered value). NINE NAMED MUTATIONS each of which must go RED: B1 cash still fed from net_margin_gbp (the split is cosmetic); B2 delta=0; B3 lambda_bill=lambda_collect=0; B4 mark path reduced to a single terminal snapshot (today's behaviour); B5 calls raised but never settled (today's behaviour); B6 IM identically 0 (today's behaviour); B7 one injected NaN mark, which must FAIL rather than return survived=True as it does today; B8 BIDIRECTIONALITY -- run against baseline history_replay and a milder shock, where the test must PASS/survive, because a test that kills in every world is not a control; B9 drop the B6 fields from the report reducer (today's behaviour) against a published-surface assertion. WHERE R15 DOES NOT REACH, stated rather than papered over: the hedge-accounting deferral (WHY the MtM loss does not hit P&L) is a modelling assumption about accounting treatment, not a mechanism a mutation can falsify -- it must be a named R10 simplification with its real-world basis cited, and its alternative (full fair-value through P&L, under which cash and P&L move together and the divergence shrinks) recorded as the thing that would falsify it. The one live switching-named module (company/pricing/switching_recommendation.py, imported by company/portal/app.py:30) is TARIFF switching between the company's own products, not industry switching. Same population and shape as the 2026-08-13 "gas industry-systems layer is eleven modules and no callers" finding; EP12's half is larger. The origin_note's "modelled the easy half" is therefore NOT a description of the company's code -- cos_process.CoSStage already runs SWITCH_REQUESTED -> OBJECTION_WINDOW -> OBJECTION_CLEARED -> FINAL_READ_REQUESTED -> FINAL_READ_RECEIVED -> SWITCH_COMPLETE with OBJECTED terminal, and erroneous_transfer.ETStatus runs OPEN -> INVESTIGATING -> RESOLVED_CORRECTED/RESOLVED_ACCEPTED -> COMPENSATION_DUE -> CLOSED. It is a description of the WORLD's code and of the seam. THE WORLD HAS NO SWITCH TO BE WRONG ABOUT: the entire exit mechanism is one Bernoulli at a term boundary (simulation/customer_events.py:139-142, retained = roll <= effective_p_retain), so (a) there is exactly ONE undifferentiated exit event -- home_move_won is rolled on ALL non-retention, so every departure in this world is a home move that may or may not be won, and a competitive switch does not exist as a distinct thing that can happen; (b) the exit is instantaneous and irreversible, with no in-flight period, gaining counterparty, objection window or reversal, so there is no state that could be wrong for a fortnight and then corrected; (c) grep -iE "erroneous|objection|failed switch|rejected_switch" over simulation/ and sim/ returns ONE hit and it is a comment. The only switching failure mode the world models is on the GAIN leg (acquisition_funnel.py, live via run_phase2b.py:79, attrites at cooling_off through ONBOARDING_TO_COOLING_OFF_SURVIVAL resi 0.80 pre / 0.92 post) -- so the company can lose a switch it is GAINING and can never lose a switch it is LOSING. COUPLED TRIAD therefore blocks L3 structurally, not for want of build effort: the company's belief would be "in flight, may be objected, may prove erroneous" and the world's truth is a boolean, so no belief-vs-truth gap is available. Same conclusion EP10 reached about UIG, from the opposite direction. THE WALL CARRIES THE CAUSE OF A GAIN AND DISCARDS THE CAUSE OF A LOSS: sim_interface.notify_acquisition carries channel ("home-move-win" vs "market-acquisition") and predecessor_id; notify_churn carries only a free-text reason -- and at the ONE live production call site (run_phase2b.py:1570) that reason is the literal constant "non-renewal", fired UNCONDITIONALLY including on the branch that four lines later (1577) establishes the departure WAS a home move. The world knows the cause at that moment and throws it away on the loss leg while preserving it on the gain leg. So the origin_note's "a switch and a tenancy change look identical from the company's side until they don't" UNDERSTATES HEAD: on the loss side they are identical always and there is no "until". Judged a fidelity gap and not the epistemic wall working (INFERRED, on the internal evidence that the sibling gain leg does carry cause and no wall doctrine distinguishes the two legs): a real supplier losing a customer to a competitor receives a registration flow naming a gaining supplier, and one losing a customer to a house move typically is not told or is told late -- distinguishable WITH LATENCY AND ERROR, which is the thing this atom exists to model. "CSS" MEANS THREE DIFFERENT THINGS IN THIS TREE, registered because it will mis-wire a future builder: saas/reporting/css_statement.py is the Consolidated Segmental Statement (SLC 19A, 712 lines, LIVE via annual_report.py:9290,9311), company/crm/css_tracker.py is the Customer Satisfaction Survey, and only company/market/css_performance_register.py is the Centralised Switching Service -- the only one of the three with live callers is the one that has nothing to do with this atom. THE CSS CUTOVER SITS INSIDE THE REPLAY WINDOW: the 2016-2025 replay crosses a regime boundary (INFERRED from the atom's own dated source, docs/design/refs/ADVISOR_RESEARCH_COUNTERPARTY_APIS_EPOCH3_2026-08-05.md, marked verified-live 2026-08-05 for the RECCo/DCC/Data-Access-Matrix facts), and the tree's only switching MESSAGE vocabulary (dtn_log.py: D0150 registration, D0301Z switch request; mpas_standing_data_correction_register.py: D0019) is the PRE-CSS DTN/D-flow regime and is dead. Exactly one constant knows about the change -- simulation/acquisition_funnel.py:76 REC_REFORM_DATE = date(2022, 7, 1), carrying its own confidence markers (M on the regime fact, L on the rates) and explicitly domestic-only -- and it is on the gain leg, the section-3 asymmetry again. THE FRAME, ordered by what unblocks what: F1 the WORLD needs a switch event with a cause, a duration and an outcome that can be other than success, before the adapter has a counterparty -- this is world work and it is where the gain ("an industry process with its own failure modes") actually lives; F2 the wall's loss primitive needs the shape its gain primitive already has, which is a SEAM change and is EP6_wall_protocol_typing, this atom's declared depends_on, OBSERVED AT LEVEL 0 -- EP12 cannot be built as a wrapper over the current seam because a single past-tense notify_churn call cannot express an in-flight reversible multi-step switch, so the declared dependency is real and correct; F3 only then is the adapter the work, and by then it is small, because the fifteen dead modules already model the company's side and the BUILD move is to wire them rather than write them again. WHAT THE ADAPTER DOES NOT NEED: REC eligibility, the Data Access Matrix and REC Code Manager confirmation gate the TRANSPORT, not a mocked adapter, a world switch event, or a measured gap -- the access class is a reason EP12 cannot reach L3 AS AN INTEGRATION, not a reason its coupled loop cannot be built (same distinction EP10 drew about the Data Services Contract; EP19 holds the qualification path itself and nothing here duplicates that register). A DEFECT FOUND AND REGISTERED NOT FIXED (SELF-INTERRUPT DISCIPLINE, and this is a doc-only lane): run_phase2b.py:1577-1589 rolls home_move_won for EVERY non-retained account but SUCCESSOR_MAP has 6 keys (C1-C6) against 20 customers, so for the other 14 a True roll takes the outer if, finds no successor, does nothing, AND never reaches the elif mandate_permits_replacement() branch -- the account is lost with no successor and no market replacement, making a True win roll a strictly WORSE outcome than a False one and depressing the realised home-move-win rate below its parameter. Staged as a worker finding. SIX OPEN ITEMS NAMED AND NOT GLOSSED (R10): the REC_REFORM_DATE value is unverified against the actual go-live and no network exists in autonomous runs to check it; the pre-2022 half of the replay window has no adapter shape at all and whether EP12 owns both regimes is a curriculum question (R13), undecidable by this pass; the gas half (Supply Point Switching) is far thinner than the electricity half and EP10 already found the gas layer dead, so the two atoms share a gas problem neither owns; W2_12_change_of_tenancy_debt_physics is at L1 verify and its world half is ALSO absent by its own words (simulation/dd_balance_book.py:74-76 -- TenancyChangeCoupler has no production caller and the SIM has no tenancy-change stream), so BOTH sides of the origin_note's coupling are missing from the world and whichever atom moves first should build the shared exit event rather than two; the 165 tests are all direct-construction and none would fail if the world never produced a switch, which is why the layer sat dead and green (not a mutation-test claim -- no control was mutated this pass); and 2026-08-05 is the freshness ceiling on every external claim. honest_holds.note:
2026-08-18 DISCOVER PASS 3, level stays 0, loop_stage stays idle (worker tick, LANE 3 idle draw). No BUILD code written, `file_scope` untouched (empty). Measured at HEAD 1f37fe393 with the map, this store file and docs/design/frame/ clean in the shared tree at draw time. Full pass appended to `docs/design/frame/EP16_ANCHORED_GENERATORS_FRAME.md` (§9-§11). Passes 1-2 took the SCHEDULING of price events (aseasonal, elec/gas at chance); this pass takes the NEGATIVE-PRICE overlay, because it is the one ScenarioParams field whose real counterpart is measurable to the half-hour from a dataset already in the tree (`sim/cache/elexon_ssp_full.json`, 2016-2024, n=3,287 complete days / 157,759 half-hours) and it lands on `baseline_2025`, the single preset pass 1 §5 showed the fidelity check CAN judge. Generated side measured through the shipped path (generate_scenario_prices -> intraday_shape.shape_day), 2026-2029 x 3 seeds.

FINDING 9 -- THE NEGATIVE-PRICE CALIBRATION MATCHES THE ONE MOMENT IT WAS FITTED TO AND INVERTS EVERY STRUCTURAL PROPERTY UNDER IT. baseline_2025 vs real: negative HOURS/yr 168.8 vs 176.4 (0.96x -- the calibration target, matched); days carrying any negative half-hour 12.5 vs 58.4 (0.21x); median negative periods on such a day 45 (22.5h) vs 4 (2h), 11x; most negative periods in one day 48/48 generated vs a real maximum EVER OBSERVED of 31/48; days with a negative DAILY MEAN 6.4/yr vs 0.67/yr (6 in 9 years), 9.6x; and the generated negative day is drawn N(-20,15) when the deepest daily mean GB has ever recorded is -16.91, so the MEAN generated negative day is deeper than the deepest real one. The mechanism is in the generator's own docstring -- "165 negative hours/year = ~7 days/year (at ~24h/day x occurrence fraction)": the model's unit is a DAILY MEAN, so the only way it can express a negative hour is to make the whole day negative, and the year's hour budget gets packed into a fifth as many days at eleven times the duration. Real negatives are a ~2-hour midday event on 58 separate days; all six real negative-mean days are low-demand high-output spring/early-summer days, shallow (-1.12 to -16.91) with 19-30 of 48 periods negative, never all 48. Two riders: (a) the upper anchor is ARITHMETICALLY UNREACHABLE -- the same docstring maps "1000 negative hours" to "28 days/year" and 28 days hold 672 hours, so the top of the cited band is bounded by the representation, not the research; (b) the component that COULD produce the real shape has no scenario dial -- intraday_shape.py's single deep-negative half-hour is `trough_base_rate: 0.02` and that module states by design it "adds NO new per-scenario dial", so the frequency of the event that actually happens is a fixed constant no preset can move while `negative_days_per_year` moves an event that does not occur. A COMPENSATING-ERROR finding, and pass 1 §5's open question made concrete: a six-moment check on daily price RETURNS cannot see any row of that table except the first.

FINDING 10 -- IN THREE OF FIVE PRESETS THE DIAL NAMED FOR NEGATIVE PRICES IS NOT WHAT PRODUCES THEM. The regime draws are unbounded Gaussians, so a low mean with a wide std emits negative daily prices with NO overlay involved. Dial vs analytic regime leak vs realised measured count: battery_saturation_2029 10.0 / 46.4 / 51.8 (dial's share 18%); stress_dunkelflaute_2027 28.0 / 27.1 / 49.4 (51%); central_2027 20.0 / 5.8 / 23.0 (78%); baseline_2025 7.0 / 0.0 / 6.4 (100%); low_renewables_2027 5.0 / 0.0 / 4.7 (100%). battery_saturation_2029 is the clean case because its comment records the intent -- `negative_days_per_year=10.0,  # batteries absorb most surpluses; fewer sustained negatives` -- reasoning that set it to the second-LOWEST dial of the five, while the preset delivers the HIGHEST realised negative-day count of all five, 5.2x its own dial, because lower_mode_std=25 against lower_mode_mean=20 puts a fifth of its lower-regime days below zero. The governing parameter is `lower_mode_std`, which is not named for negatives, is not documented as a negative-price lever, and cannot be read off the preset table without evaluating a normal CDF. Distinct from finding 9 and distinct from the pass-2 provenance item: a parameter-provenance control would PASS this preset (the dial is sourced and reasoned) and still miss that it controls 18% of the outcome it names. LATENT, NOT LIVE, and stated as such: `negative_price_floor` is applied only on the overlay branch and never to the regime draw, but observed minima over 3 seeds were -66.22 and -69.67, both inside the -75 floor -- an asymmetry recorded, not a defect claimed.

FINDING 11 -- THE NEGATIVE OVERLAY SILENTLY OVERWRITES THE DUNKELFLAUTE OVERLAY, REPLACING A SCARCITY EVENT WITH ITS PHYSICAL OPPOSITE. The two overlays are applied in sequence onto independently drawn index sets, last-write-wins, so a day scheduled as both becomes a deep negative. Measured by re-deriving both index sets exactly as the generator does, 5 presets x 3 seeds: 42 of 777 scheduled dunkelflaute days overwritten (5.4%), and 8.1% inside stress_dunkelflaute_2027 (10.0 days per draw) and 8.3% in central_2027. A dunkelflaute is a still, dark spell -- precisely the state in which negative prices CANNOT form, since negative prices are a renewable-SURPLUS phenomenon, confirmed on the real side by finding 9 where all six negative-mean days are low-demand high-output days. The generator takes its highest-price event and on 8% of those days replaces it with the one event the same weather excludes: R10 ABSURDITY CLASS, not a tuning error. Second consequence for the record: `dunkelflaute_events_per_year` silently under-delivers by that fraction, and PASS 2'S §7 SHARED-DAY COUNTS WERE COMPUTED ON THE SCHEDULED INDEX SETS -- the realised elec/gas coupling is very slightly lower still than the at-chance figure reported there. §7's conclusion is unchanged (already at chance); its numbers should be read as scheduled-set numbers.

CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: passes 1 and 2 both cited `docs/reports/run_history.json` as the evidence that no forward-scenario run has ever been published. That file does not exist at this HEAD. The conclusion is unchanged and now rests on a stronger check -- `scenario_name` appears in ZERO of the 5,281 JSON files under docs/reports/, and run_output_latest.json has no such key.

WHAT PASS 3 ADDS TO THE ITEM LIST: item 4 ("define what anchored means for a world that never happened") splits into 4a PARAMETER PROVENANCE (pass 2 §8 -- every generating parameter carries its source), 4b DIAL AUTHORITY (finding 10, new -- every parameter named for a quantity must be shown to be the dominant lever on it; provenance passes battery_saturation_2029 and still misses it), and 4c PHENOMENON SHAPE NOT PARAMETER VALUE (finding 9, new -- daily-mean granularity cannot express a 2-hour midday event, so no value of any parameter fixes it; the first item on EP16's list that is neither a number nor a wiring job, and the one the six-moment check is structurally blind to). Plus a sixth top-level item: FIX THE OVERLAY PRECEDENCE (finding 11), smallest on the list, and the third live-code defect this FRAME has found alongside intraday_shape.py's false "already director-owned" guarantee and the false gas-coupling comments.

R12: no published number tuned; latent on the check above. R13: no curriculum value authored, proposed or changed -- findings 9 and 11 are BASELINE FIDELITY (the shape and physics of negative prices are properties of the real world, measured blind to company P&L) and finding 10 names a dial as non-authoritative over its own quantity without proposing a value for it; per-preset severity stays the director's. QUEUED NOT FIXED (self-interrupt discipline): the overlay precedence, the unfloored regime leak and the whole-day negative representation all live in sim/scenario/bimodal_generator.py, outside this atom's empty file_scope, and belong to the scenario-generator path with W1_2.

The origin note prescribes: "build them as one message model with two transports, or the
mock has no oracle." Read against the tree, the model that exists cannot be that model.

`tools/meter_read_port.py::MeterReadMessage` (field-identical to
`simulation/meter_reads.py::MeterReadEvent`, by design -- the port's docstring calls itself
"a SHAPE change to already-correct data"):

    customer_id, period_end, meter_type, delay_days, status,
    estimated_consumption_kwh, true_consumption_kwh,
    consecutive_estimated_count, forced_catch_up

Four of those nine are SUPPLIER BOOKKEEPING, not counterparty data: `status`
("actual"|"estimated"), `estimated_consumption_kwh`, `consecutive_estimated_count` and
`forced_catch_up` (the 12-month back-billing cap). A DUIS service-request response returns a
register value; an n3rgy pull returns a midnight index read plus a half-hourly usage file
(advisor research, verified 2026-08-05). NEITHER COUNTERPARTY CAN RETURN "ESTIMATED" -- an
estimate is what a supplier does when a counterparty returns nothing.

HOW MUCH OF THE SEAM THAT IS, on the live artefact: 469 of 1,600 messages (29.31%) carry
`status: "estimated"`, every one of them with a non-null `estimated_consumption_kwh`. Split
by meter type: 326 traditional, 143 smart.

AND THE ESTIMATE IS COMPUTED WORLD-SIDE. `simulation/meter_reads.py::simulate_read` builds
it as `statistics.mean(trailing_actuals_kwh[-3:])` (`ESTIMATE_TRAILING_WINDOW = 3`) and
returns it inside the event. The company does not compute it: `company/billing/
monthly_bill_assembly.py:406` threads its own trailing actuals INTO the world call and line
484 reads `event.estimated_consumption_kwh` straight back out. "Average of your last N
periods" is the supplier's own commercial technique -- a real supplier is free to change it
without telling anyone -- and it currently lives in world code.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ATOM, stated plainly because it inverts the atom's own promise: at
accession a real DUIS adapter has NO estimate to return, so the estimation must move
company-side. That is a computation relocating across the wall -- not a transport swap. The
`name:` field's "the eventual swap is transport-only" is not achievable from here, and would
become achievable only if the message model were re-cut FIRST.

RECOMMENDATION, acted on by recording it rather than asking (NEVER_ASK_WITHOUT_RECOMMENDING):
EP8's first BUILD task is the CUT, not the adapter -- separate (a) what the transport
returns (a register/index read, or an error) from (b) what the supplier's billing engine
concludes (actual vs estimated, the estimate itself, the consecutive-run and back-billing
state). The origin note's "one message model" instinct is right; the model it must be one of
is the COUNTERPARTY'S, and today's is the supplier's.

2016-01-31 to 2025-06-07 (3,416 days). The n3rgy contract the advisor verified is ONCE DAILY
PER METER, which over the same customers and the same span is 64,904 pulls -- 40.6x the
messages this seam carries. That is not a volume quibble; it is where the physics lives:

- "MISSING DAYS STAY MISSING UNLESS RE-REQUESTED" -- named in EP9's own record as the
  fidelity gold and "the part most likely to be smoothed away" -- IS NOT REPRESENTABLE. A
  monthly message has no day to be missing. The only latency carrier on the seam is
  `delay_days`, one scalar per customer-period (live range 0..68).
- A DUIS billing-register read returns a cumulative REGISTER INDEX at an instant; this
  message carries a PERIOD CONSUMPTION. Consumption has to be derived from index deltas,
  and the whole class of defects that lives in that derivation -- register rollover,
  meter exchange, index regression, a read pair straddling a tariff change -- is not
  merely unimplemented here, it is unrepresentable in the current field set.

So the atom's honest granularity target is per-meter-per-day index reads, and the billing
period becomes a thing the SUPPLIER derives. That is the same cut finding 1 arrives at from

prerequisite.

honest_holds.atom_name: Deliverable 3: growth from the opening book is GRADUAL AND EARNED -- won and lost against the market through the acquisition physics already built, never incremented. AMENDED 2026-08-15 (DISCOVER, worker tick) because the original wording was vacuous: it asked only that a world configuration in which the book SHRINKS be demonstrated, and at HEAD the book can ONLY shrink -- acquisition is replacement-only and can fail, so book size is monotonically non-increasing -- which means that test passes on unbuilt code, an R15 fail-open. The DIRECTION OF THE CURVE is not the test; the IDENTITY OF THE MECHANISM is -- "won and lost against the market" is not satisfied by a book that goes up and down, only by a book whose up and whose down are the SAME contest. Both legs must therefore come from the same contested mechanism, proven by a NULL CONTROL: (b1) with the arrival stream held FIXED, a change to the company's own market position alone must move book size in BOTH directions; and (b2) with the arrival stream EMPTIED, the book must still be able to grow. honest_holds.note:
2026-08-24 PB3 ADD-PATH BUILT, and this entry is the cost of the way it was built. `net_new_acquisition.homes_in_market` now sizes each year's in-play market from the real DESNZ-calibrated switching series (`market_switching_propensity.market_switching_multiplier`) instead of the flat PROSPECTS_PER_YEAR constant, so 2022's crisis (0.44x) and 2016's peak competition (2.17x) are different worlds to acquire in. That is exit (a)'s ADD leg wired, and it is the SAME constant the LOSS leg reads in `customer_events` -- which is the director's 2026-08-17 anti-goal-seek guard made structural: opening the market to win more customers opens it equally for the ones already on the book.

THE SIMPLIFICATION, `observed-with-evidence`: the multiplier can only THIN the market, never widen it. It is capped at `prospects_per_year`, so ABOVE 1.0 IT IS INERT and every year from 2016-2020 sizes identically to 2024 despite the series saying the market was up to 2.17x more open. In a peak-competition year this model therefore UNDERSTATES how winnable the market was, and any read of 'the company failed to grow in 2016' inherits that understatement rather than measuring it.

WHY IT IS CAPPED rather than left free. Prospects are drawn `iter_prospects(year, n=prospects_per_year)` out of a stock partition PB2 splits with the Profile-B trickle -- campaign takes the head, trickle the tail. An uncapped 2.17x asks for 869 homes from a 400-home partition and does not get them: measured before the cap, 2016 reported 600 quotes_issued against 400 actual wins on an ALWAYS-WIN funnel, i.e. a published growth figure claiming quotes the run never issued and never billed. Uncapping would also make the campaign's slice depend on the year's multiplier, which is exactly the boundary PB2 fixed to make 'won, never assigned' measurable.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: widen the stock partition itself so a peak year has more homes to draw, which is a PB2-boundary change (campaign/trickle split) and not a number to move from inside this module. Until then the honest reading of the growth curve is that thin years are modelled and rich years are clipped. Guarded by `test_the_market_can_only_be_THINNED_never_widened_past_the_stock_partition` and, end-to-end, by `test_every_quote_the_run_REPORTS_is_a_quote_it_actually_BILLED`, which fails on the exact 600-vs-400 defect above.

NOT CLAIMED: exit (b) is NOT discharged by this. 'A world in which the book GROWS and one in which it SHRINKS, from the same mechanism' needs the net of wins against churn at the population level; this atom's half is the ADD leg being real and market-driven. The level is not moved on the strength of this entry.

honest_holds.note:
2026-09-03 L0->L2 SELF-CERTIFIED (worker tick, drawn as lane-0 delivery rather than by atom id; ledger row in docs/observability/gate_authorizations.jsonl). THE DRAWN FINDING WAS HALF WRONG AND THE WRONG HALF IS THE MORE USEFUL ONE. The item said `site/capabilities/index.html` contains zero occurrences of "could not react", "cannot react" or "two internal policies" and concluded the page publishes the baseline comparison unbounded. The grep is exactly right and the conclusion does not follow: THE BOUND IS NOT MARKUP. It is composed clause-by-clause by `tools/generate_value_arms_data.py::_reaction_sentence` from `_market_reaction`, which drives `simulation/competitor_reference.py` at three real dates, ships in `value_arms.json`, and is assigned into `#arms-market` by the door's own script. MEASURED, not reasoned: fetching https://poesys.net/capabilities/ and its four live feeds and driving the door's own boot path with them renders, today, "What the world could do about either arm. These are two of our own pricing policies, run through the same world... The market DOES defend... Nothing contests the ceiling... Read the comparison as an internal one." That is C2's bound, on the deployed surface, and it has been there since the probe landed on 2026-08-28. The atom sat at level 0 for two consecutive stretches against work that had already met its page half, because the cell was being graded by a grep of static HTML against a sentence the page composes at runtime.
WHAT WAS GENUINELY MISSING is the half the atom's own gain clause calls binding -- "R11 binds hardest here: done means fetching the LIVE deployed surface and asserting the sentence renders" -- a control that goes RED if it stops. Neither existing control is it, and both were checked rather than assumed. (1) `site/test_the_baseline_comparison_reaches_the_reader.py` asserts the property well and its subject is the REPO door driven with the REPO feed; it is green on a tree that deploys nothing and green while the edge serves a stale copy, which is the outage `live_pixel_verify.cache_bust` documents at eight hours and climbing. (2) `site/live_pixel_verify.py` DOES fetch the live surface and structurally cannot see this defect: `verify_door` grades with `if not text: continue`, so an element the door left empty leaves the checked population before any assertion runs. `site/test_door_render_functions_are_wired.py:18` already records that shape in terms -- "grades only elements the page's script WROTE... fail-open for PARTIAL render" -- and an `#arms-market` that renders nothing is precisely a partial render. So the one live control we own would have reported the door OK while the comparison went out unbounded.
BUILT: `site/test_the_published_bound_reaches_the_live_reader.py`. It fetches the deployed door, reads the feed urls out of the bytes the host actually served, fetches those, drives the door's own boot path (`site/_live_harness.mjs`) and judges `#arms-market`. The judgement is factored into a pure `_judge(rendered, reaction)` so it can be mutated with no network at all -- a judge only exercisable through a fetch could only be proven able to fail by breaking the live site.
KEYED TO THE PROPERTY, NEVER TO TODAY'S SENTENCE, and this atom is the reason that rule exists. C2's own wording was HALF FALSE within half an hour of the director writing it, when `simulation/competitor_reference.py` landed and gave the market a defence. Putting the drawn item's literal string on the page TODAY would have published a correction to a defect the world had already half fixed. So what is asserted is that the reader is told the comparison is internal, and that every clause the page states about what the world could do AGREES leg by leg with the live feed's own probe. Both legs can flip -- the ceiling leg is unbuilt and will land -- and nothing needs editing when they do.
R15, MUTATION-PROVEN AGAINST THE BYTES POESYS.NET ACTUALLY SERVED, not against a fixture: took the served html, replaced `$("arms-market").innerHTML =` with a dead assignment, re-drove the door, and `_judge` returned "#arms-market rendered NOTHING on the deployed page..." (unmutated: CLEAN). Second live mutation: stripped `market_reaction` from the served feed -- the door correctly rendered its stated-absence fallback and `_judge` still returned a defect, because a bound nobody could establish is not a bound anybody has checked. FAIL-CLOSED proven by pointing `CANONICAL_HOST` at an unresolvable host: `Failed: the deployed door could not be reached... reported as a FAILURE and never skipped`. Four further mutations run offline against the pure judge (empty panel; the word "internal" removed; C2's original stale wording served while the probe reports a defending market; an unavailable probe), each red, with `test_the_mutation_subject_is_itself_clean` as the vacuity guard so none of them can pass for the wrong reason. 7 passed at this commit.
THE COST IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. `live_pixel_verify` declined to be a test on the ground that "a network-dependent control in the commit path would wedge every offline commit". That argument was weighed, not inherited: it was made for a crawler over twelve doors and every feed each fetches, where a blip costs the whole gate. This is one door, one panel, four feeds, and the atom it discharges says a live check that passes when the network is down discharges nothing. The reversal, if it starts wedging offline work, is written into the module docstring: move the two live rungs behind an opt-in and leave `_judge` and its mutation rungs where they are.
FILE_SCOPE CORRECTED IN THE SAME LANDING, and it is the finding in miniature. The scope named `tools/generate_capabilities_door.py` and `tests/tools/`; neither produces or verifies the bound. A file_scope pointing away from the code is how an atom sits at 0 beside work that has already met it -- the same reading error as the grep. Now: `site/capabilities/`, `tools/generate_value_arms_data.py` and the two door tests under `site/`.
HELD AT 2 AND NOT PROPOSED HIGHER, with the residuals named rather than absorbed: (a) THE FAIL-OPEN IN `live_pixel_verify.verify_door` IS UNFIXED. `if not text: continue` still drops every empty element on all twelve doors; this landing covers ONE panel on ONE door by naming it. Fixing it at the class needs the blast radius measured first -- doors legitimately leave `querySelector` stubs empty -- so it is filed, not absorbed. That is R10 debt and it is the next thing anyone reading this should pick up. (b) The two live rungs are the only network-dependent pytest in the tree. If the gate's selection picks them up on an offline machine they will red, correctly and inconveniently. (c) The bound is verified; the FIGURES it bounds are separately known stale -- the arms ran 2026-08-31 and the departure level anchor has been re-fitted twice since. That is the lane-0 item 1 this one was sequenced ahead of, deliberately, because a page with fresh figures and no bound is worse than today's. It remains open.

honest_holds.note:
2026-08-12 BUILT, level 0 -> 2 (worker tick, self-certified with the evidence below per R16). Part 2 of DIRECTOR_RULING_THE_PORTAL_IS_A_WALL_EXHIBIT_2026-08-12. site/customers/index.html stops calling itself a Customer Portal and becomes the wall's own exhibit: one household's own view side by side with what the company knows and what only the simulation knows.
THE MECHANISM, AND WHY IT IS NOT PROSE. The ruling's non-negotiable was that the side-declaration be STRUCTURAL -- "if a new panel can be added to this page without declaring which side of the wall it sits on, nothing has been built, only written down", and it named the existing honesty-wall notes as exactly the prose version of the gap. So no tab renderer emits panel markup any more. Each returns a LIST of panel(side, title, body) objects and layoutPanels() is the SOLE writer of `.wall-panel` markup; panel() throws on a missing or unknown side and layoutPanels() throws again on anything reaching it that is neither a declared panel nor explicitly-marked chrome. That alone would still be walk-past-able by hand-building a card around the helper, so the second half is a STRUCTURAL GUARD on the rendered markup (site/customers/test_wall_exhibit.py::test_no_content_block_renders_outside_a_declared_panel): an HTML scanner walks every tab in every view and fails on any content block -- card, kpi-grid, accounts-grid, chart-wrap, bill-sum, timeline-list -- that inherits no declared side. Nav chrome carries none of those classes, which is why chrome legitimately needs no side and content cannot avoid one. Placeholders the page fills in AFTER layout (bills-section, usage-section, cashflow-kpis, cashflow-kpis-company, forecast-cashflow-body) are checked separately to sit inside a declared panel, or the guard would be bypassable by injecting into a bare div.
THE FIGURES ACTUALLY MOVED, they were not merely relabelled. The top-of-page money grid used to render billed, banked, balance, lifetime net, cost-to-serve, churn risk AND a SIM satisfaction score as one undifferentiated row of tiles; it is now three panels on three sides (cust-money / cust-value / cust-sim), and the who-they-are grid split into the customer's own account facts (cust-who) and the supplier's classification of them -- segment, occupancy, vulnerability flag, engagement (cust-classify). Timeline split: the events a household lived through stay customer-side, while the CAUSAL EFFECT attached to each event moved to a SIM panel alongside the reaction chain, since a causal attribution is ground truth no supplier could read. Risk split into the customer's own outstanding balance and the supplier's churn probability / expected lifetime / pricing action. Cashflow split into billed-vs-collected (customer) and cost-to-serve / net contribution / forecast (company).
THE CUSTOMER-EYE VIEW IS A REAL VIEW. A three-way selector (Both sides / The customer's side / Behind the wall) filters by OMITTING panels from the DOM, not by hiding them with CSS -- so "the customer cannot see this" is true of the rendered document, not just of its styling. headline_caveats: DILUTED: the inference ran on 34 of 200 premises (83% carry no information about it). Improvement over the register is +0.0227 as published and +0.1233 where the inference ran; the published figure moves with EPC lodgement coverage even when the estimator does not.

ONE-SIGNED (epc): the belief is under-stated in 126 of 200 decided premises (sign-test p=0.0003, signed mean +19.6%). The company is wrong about the STOCK in a fixed direction, not merely imprecise about houses; the |gap| headline cannot see this.

SKEWED (epc): that count and that average point OPPOSITE ways — under-stated on 126 of 200 premises, yet a signed mean of +19.6%. A minority of large errors outweighs the majority of small ones, so a supplier reading the mean would target different houses from one reading the median. Read the line above as a majority, not an average.

MIRROR INCONCLUSIVE: the panel mirror did NOT move the money verdict off inferred, and that null carries no weight here — 73% of the mirror's movement in the deciding margin is reproduced by a null panel carrying the same re-weighting with NO sign flip in it (GBP 230 of 314 per PANEL premise — both means are over all 200, not over the movers, 95% interval [36%, 90%], across the 18 of 200 premises the mirror moved; the totals-based rule would have said 90%, with 40% of the mirror's and 25% of the null's movement cancelling inside its two sums), and this panel cannot resolve which side of the 50% band that share sits on, so 'the instrument is clean' is not something it measured, so 'no composition effect' is not a finding on this population.

CONFIDENCE-BOUGHT: swapping the two arms' ERROR BARS and bases — every point estimate untouched, so both accuracy gaps are unchanged by construction — moves the money verdict from inferred to epc. The arm that forgoes less is the arm ALLOWED TO ACT more often (declined-where-value-existed 89 on the register vs 73 on the posterior), which is a claim about the company's confidence, not about its accuracy. This is the sense in which the two headlines disagree: they are not two views of one quantity.

belief.belief_resolution_caveat: RESOLUTION IS THIS BOOK'S EVENT SPAN (atom D27, measured 2026-08-10, seeds 7/11/23). Both belief dimensions read ONE company parameter -- the DD/rail failure lookback window `_arrears_risk_belief` counts inside -- and an event can only change side if the window falls BELOW its age. AND WHAT THIS FIGURE ITSELF RESOLVES (atom D33): `belief` publishes no readable difference for any memory error smaller than 310d of forgetting, measured through its own shipped scorer on the offline scenario (n=300, seeds 7/11/23, at the 4dp THIS figure's own consumer renders IT at -- atom D34; the five published figures do not share one) -- against `belief_population_mix` 314d, so the belief figures do NOT share a resolution and the number below is a bound on the book, not this figure's sensitivity. On a live population no sweep has visited, only that bound is measured here. This book: 655 observed failure events, oldest 3438d before `as_of`, against a company window of 6000d -- SATURATED, with 2562d of headroom. No event in this book can fall out of that window, so this figure cannot distinguish this company from one that NEVER forgets a failure -- the direction that keeps a recovered customer in collections -- and NO memory error smaller than 2563d of forgetting can move ANY figure here, because no observed event changes side inside it (a BOUND on this book, never a figure's own resolution -- atom D33). A zero here is not proof the company remembers the right amount; it is mostly proof this book is shorter than its memory. AND THE OTHER EDGE (atom D29): the youngest observed failure is 30d old, so a company whose memory runs 29d or less counts NOTHING -- every such supplier, down to total amnesia, publishes one figure as well. This number resolves a memory error only BETWEEN those two edges.
belief.scenario_constant_census_caveat: THE BAND IS THE BOOK'S LENGTH (atom D30, H27 Expert Hour #12). This book's INVOICES span ages between 30d and 3469d -- a band 3439d wide, and a band is a property of how long the book is, never a sensitivity of the instrument. THE BELIEF DIMENSIONS' OWN BAND IS SMALLER, and is the one that sets their edges: they read OBSERVED FAILURES only, which here span 30d to 3438d over 655 events. THAT IS NOT THE INVOICE SPAN: a failure has to LAND on the extreme invoice for the two to coincide, and on this book it did not -- so the constants below attribute the INVOICE band and the belief band above is measured here, not attributed. This is NOT the offline scenario's book, so the census's constants (['AS_OF_BUFFER_DAYS', 'BILLING_CYCLE_SPREAD_DAYS', 'N_PERIODS', 'PERIOD_SPACING_DAYS']) do not attribute these edges -- the band above is measured here and owned by whatever placed this population's invoices. AND THE SCORED COMPANY SITS OUTSIDE IT: it holds 6000d of memory, 2531d past the top of the band, so every belief figure here is read at a point where the one company parameter these dimensions depend on is inert by construction (reported, never tuned -- R12).

components.drift_resolution_caveat: RESOLUTION IS WHICH CASES THIS HEADLINE COUNTS (atoms D28 and D31, measured 2026-08-13, cause corrected 2026-08-14 on a grid whose density AND EXTENT are derived from the book and not from this register, seeds 7/11/23). This headline is SET MEMBERSHIP over TWO COUNTED POPULATIONS -- `S`, the true failures, and `N`, the never-flaggable negatives. A company's terms error moves it only where that error carries an invoice across the grace line AND that invoice is in `S` or `N`: crossing the line is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT. DO NOT RUN THAT BACKWARDS -- an unmoved number does NOT mean nothing crossed. Offline scenario: the reading SATURATES below -6d and above +82d -- every supplier whose terms are more wrong than that publishes ONE figure, so a supplier a week short on its terms (the direction that flags a paying customer as in arrears and posts the dunning letter) is indistinguishable here from one 20 days short. THE TWO EDGES ARE TWO KINDS OF OBJECT and only one may be relied on (atom D26, 2026-08-19). BELOW is ARITHMETIC over the grace window -- -(DEFAULT_RECONCILIATION_GRACE_DAYS + 1) -- so it holds in any book, differentially proven over grace in {2,5,10}. ABOVE is a DRAW: it is this book's luckiest case and NOT the book running out (at the edge the oldest true failure is still inside its line), so it is scoped to 7/11/23 and must not be quoted over another population. In between it is quantised, not continuous: 14 further groups of companies publish one number each {-4,-3}, {+0,+1}, {+6,+7}, {+9,+10}, {+11,+12,+13}, {+17,+18,+19,+20,+21,+22,+23,+24}, {+28,+29}, {+44,+45}, {+61,+62}, {+65,+66,+67}, {+68,+69}, {+72,+73,+74}, {+76,+77,+78}, {+80,+81}. AND THE CAUSE IS THIS HEADLINE'S DENOMINATORS, NOT THE BOOK'S PLACEMENT (measured 2026-08-14): of the 86 adjacent pairs of companies in here, the flagged set steps at 61-63 on the EXCLUDED band -- invoices paid late but past grace, which the company was RIGHT to chase, counted in neither `S` nor `N` by the D10/D11 rule -- and at only 32-38 on the two populations this figure counts. At 34-40 pairs the company's flagged set moves and this number does not. The book is NOT thin beside the grace line; what is thin is the part of that traffic this headline can see, so a reshape that merely puts more invoices beside the line would not move the resolution at all (atom D28_the_detection_gap_is_quantised_by_this_books_placement). AND THE BAND IS THE READING DATE'S, NOT THE INSTRUMENT'S (atom D26_detection_grace_line_has_no_book_beside_it): the smallest company terms error this headline resolves is +2..+8d at the SHIPPED `as_of` and +1..+2d on the same books read at `last_due + DEFAULT_RECONCILIATION_GRACE_DAYS` -- the earliest date every invoice has reached its own grace line -- with every as_of-invariant figure bit-identical across 10 seeds. The published number is read at the SHIPPED date, so the wider band is the one that applies to it. Do not read a movement in this number as days of company error, and do not read a zero as accurate flagging. Residual owned by D28_the_detection_gap_is_quantised_by_this_books_placement.
components.exclusion_reason: cases in NEITHER direction's population: a payment that eventually succeeded but arrived more than 5 days (the reconciliation grace) after its due date really was unpaid past grace, so flagging it was correct and counting it as a false flag would score the company down for being right; an unresolved dispute is not a settled success either; and a record carrying no `days_late` truth is UNKNOWN, never assumed paid on time.
components.recon_saturation_caveat: SATURATION (atom D31, measured on a grid derived from the BOOK, n=300, seeds [7, 11, 23]): resolution is not the whole real line. The first-knowledge DATE reading resolves the company day for day down to -19d and no further -- a detector that would fire before the invoice was ISSUED is read at the issue date, which is `PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS + DEFAULT_RECONCILIATION_GRACE_DAYS` and a bound on what any supplier can know. The SET reading behind the published detection gap saturates BELOW -6d, where every company has already flagged every invoice and the gap is the no-skill 0.5, and ABOVE +82d, where nothing further is detected before `as_of`. Between them it is quantised, not continuous: movement in these headlines is not readable as days of company error outside the runs stamped beside it. R12: a diagnostic, never a target. AND THE UPPER EDGE IS A PROPERTY OF THE DRAW, NOT OF THE BOOK'S SHAPE (atom D28). The +82d above was measured on ONE draw size (n=300, seeds [7, 11, 23]); across 30 books -- same one-cycle spread, same `as_of`, same grace line, same terms, only how many customers were drawn -- it moves +49..+88, and on the largest draws there is no upper saturation inside the swept grid at all. THE BAND STAMPED BESIDE THIS NUMBER IS THIS BOOK'S OWN, derived from its 9546 scored cases: -6d to +3040d. Only the LOWER edge is a bound -- -6 is the closed form `-(DEFAULT_RECONCILIATION_GRACE_DAYS + 1)`, attained by any invoice paid on its due date and invariant on all 30. The upper edge is attained by the single luckiest case, a non-DD failure never covered inside the book; the 420 scored cases the DD channel holds flagged at every drift set no edge at all. AND THE RUNS THE SENTENCE ABOVE DEFERS TO ARE THIS BOOK'S OWN, NOT THE REGISTER'S (atom D28). The 16 runs declared there were measured at n=300, seeds [7, 11, 23] and on build_scenario's own `_STRESS_MIX` -- and the STRESS MIX is the axis this quantisation lives on, which is why neither the grid sweep nor the draw-size axis could ever have found it. A book pinning every customer to one stress tier has a hole in `days_late`, and since `k*` on a negative is `days_late - grace`, a hole in `days_late` is a hole in the resolution: on the `moderate`-pinned book 6 of the 7 runs declared inside [-10, 40] are read APART, and on the all-high book this module itself builds the baseline company sits in a run 7 days wide against a declared 2. THIS BOOK publishes 122 run(s) over its own grid (-20..+3465), and the baseline company sits in NO run at all -- its reading is distinct from both neighbours. Movement in this headline is not readable as days of company error inside that run.

remittance_attribution.counterfactual: the SAME world -- same payment outcomes, same clearing dates, same bills -- observed by a company whose every credit carries its invoice remittance reference, so `AccountLedger.allocate` never falls back to oldest-first. `attributed` = actual minus that.

discrimination.reading: 5 of 5 measure(s) carrying a non-zero error read attributed == actual. THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE OBSERVATION CHANNEL, NOT EVIDENCE THAT THIS SUBTRACTION DISCRIMINATES (atom D17). Every successful payment in this world delivers its credit to BOTH books, and the never-flaggable band (D16) has already removed every invoice the company was right to carry as owed -- so the only mechanism left that can make the company believe a within-grace-settled invoice overdue is the oldest-first misallocation the counterfactual removes. Read it as 'the channel is complete on this population', never as 'the counterfactual was tested and passed'. What DOES test it is an injected belief error no invoice reference can cure -- suppress the DELIVERY of a credit and the shadow company overstates arrears too, so the attributed share falls below 1.0: tests/background/test_live_payment_triad.py::test_R15_the_counterfactual_does_not_attribute_an_injected_non_allocation_error.

pairs.note: LIVE per-run coupled-triad gap (W2_11 payment TRUTH -> W4_4 seam -> D5 consumer belief, measured in-run by run_phase2b). HEADLINE = DD/non-DD failure DETECTION gap (fraction of true payment failures the company does not BELIEVE unresolved as at the measurement date -- NOT, as this note said until 2026-08-09, failures it never observes: D10 measured every truly-failed case being flagged on time at due+grace, and the residual is cases the company detected and then UN-flagged when a later ambiguous non-DD payment was allocated oldest-first onto the failed invoice, Clayton's Case, atom D8. The no-remittance blind spot is real but is not what this number counts). READ THE HEADLINE AS RECONCILIATION-DETERMINED ALONE (D10): `flagged_set` is a UNION and deleting the DD-observation channel leaves it bit-identical -- what that channel buys is EARLIER detection, reported in days beside it. RESHAPED 2026-08-09 (atom D11) -- THIS HEADLINE IS NOT COMPARABLE WITH ANY LEDGER ENTRY WRITTEN BEFORE THAT DATE, and the discontinuity is a fix, not a drift. The H27 Expert Hour measured two defects in the old figure and both are now closed at the measure rather than caveated in prose. (1) It was an as_of ARTEFACT: the truth (`result == 'failed'`) does not move with the clock but the belief was held AT the measurement date, so holding company and world fixed and moving only that date walked the figure ~+70% over 60 days. The population is now EVER-FLAGGED -- a detection is a fact about the day it happened, whatever a later oldest-first allocation did to the invoice -- and the as_of sweep is flat. (2) It counted ONE ERROR DIRECTION: a company flagging EVERY invoice scored a perfect 0.0. The headline is now the BALANCED error of both directions on their own denominators, so both degenerate strategies score g0 = 0.5. detection balanced error 0.0709 [0.5 = every prevalence-blind rule, incl. flagging everything] (missed_failure_rate 0.0000 over 655 truly-failed, false_flag_rate 0.1417 = 1260 of 8891 never-flaggable cases wrongly flagged = the wrongful-dunning exposure; 1488 case(s) in neither population: cases in NEITHER direction's population: a payment that eventually succeeded but arrived more than 5 days (the reconciliation grace) after its due date really was unpaid past grace, so flagging it was correct and counting it as a false flag would score the company down for being right; an unresolved dispute is not a settled success either; and a record carrying no `days_late` truth is UNKNOWN, never assumed paid on time.). The retired recall-only figure is NOT restated: it was scored over a different flagged population, so no arithmetic on these sets reproduces it. Companion per-dimension gaps: belief balanced error 0.1271 [0.5 = every severity-blind rule, incl. right mix / wrong accounts]; under-called severity 0.2541 (46 of 181, mean 2.30 steps); over-called severity 0.0000 (0 of 153); per-case disagreement 0.1833 (46 of 251) [RESHAPED 2026-08-10, atom D19, and NOT comparable with the belief figure any earlier ledger entry carries: that was a population TV distance, which permuting which account holds which severity belief left bit-identical (0.0713 -> 0.0713 while per-case agreement fell 0.9287 -> 0.6432), so the degenerate 'right mix, every individual wrong' scored exactly what the real company scored. The TV figure is not deleted -- it is published as belief_population_mix 0.1833, the question it was always answering]; detection latency 2.48 days mean (without the DD-observation channel 5.00 days -- the channel buys 2.52 days EARLIER detection on 420 of 655 dated cases, while moving the set-membership detection gap by exactly zero); 0 of 655 true failures never detected at all; ageing displacement 0.439 buckets, BALANCED over both directions [no baseline; not a 0-1 ratio] (understated_arrears_rate 0.2809 over 655 truly-overdue, overstated_arrears_rate 0.0129 over 8891 truly-current = the ageing-report overstatement at as_of, NOT the wrongful-dunning exposure (atom D16); the headline's two halves: mean_bucket_displacement 0.843 buckets of UNDER-dating over the truly-overdue and mean_overstatement_displacement 0.035 buckets of OVER-ageing over the truly-current -- the headline is their mean and cannot say which direction it came from (atom D22); 1488 case(s) in neither population: cases in NEITHER ageing population (atom D16, carrying D11's rule across from the detection dimension of this same instrument): a payment that eventually succeeded but arrived more than 5 days (the reconciliation grace) after its due date really WAS unpaid past grace, so the company carrying it as owed was CORRECT even though the truth bucket at `as_of` reads `current`; an unresolved dispute is not a settled success either; and a record carrying no `days_late` truth is UNKNOWN, never assumed paid on time. Until this band existed, 94 of this dimension's 101 false ageings were cases its sibling dimension holds the company was RIGHT about.) The three measures above each carry the denominator they are about; the displacement carries none at all]; allocation honestly dropped (metric-shape mismatch). pairs.baseline_desc: no-skill = assign every account the MEAN realised lifetime margin OF THE GRADED POPULATION (GBP 100.20); g0 = that predictor's mean absolute error (GBP 269.65). gap>1 means the company's per-customer CLV carries less information than that mean. error_decomposition.reading: share of the headline one scalar absorbs = the share NOT explained by per-account error. Fitted in-sample: an attribution, never a skill estimate and never a correction to apply (R12).

hazard_calibration.reading: `believed_over_realised` above 1 means the company thinks the customer is likelier to leave than they proved to be, which makes its believed tenure -- and therefore its CLV -- too SHORT, not too long. Compare `mean_believed_tenure_years` with `implied_realised_mean_tenure_years` for the portfolio-level direction. Buckets with small `decisions` carry a realised rate that is mostly noise; `decisions` is published so a reader can see which rows are worth reading. R12: diagnostic, never a target.

lifetime_level.reading: `hazard_is_constant_across_graded_population` true means the tenure horizon contributed NO per-account variation to the graded CLV -- every ranking it produced came from the margin term alone. Recovered by inverting the published `tenure_expected`/`contract_term` ratio, which depends on the hazard alone; no company-side private state is read. R12: diagnostic, never a target.

population_selection.reading: The graded population is selected ON THE OUTCOME -- an account is counted only once its life has ENDED. Where the two populations differ in realised value, a perfectly calibrated estimator scores as a uniform over-estimate, so `error_decomposition.best_single_scale` cannot be read as an estimator fault without this row beside it. The excluded side is still accruing, so `like_for_like_excluded_over_graded` is a LOWER BOUND. Read the like-for-like ratio, not the whole-book one: segments differ by orders of magnitude in this book. R12: diagnostic, never a target.

components.truth_window_bias: realised total spans the WHOLE lifetime; the belief is taken at the first year-end snapshot. Truth is therefore measured over a longer window than the belief forecasts, which flatters an over-estimating belief -- the headline is conservative for those cases. No per-account-per-year margin is published, so the pre-snapshot slice cannot be removed.

pairs.note: Point-in-time backtest of a company CLV belief against realised lifetime margin, over accounts whose life COMPLETED inside the run. WHOSE BELIEF: the graded field is `three_horizon_clv_snapshots` -- EP1's OWN estimator (company/analytics/clv_three_horizon.py), recorded at each year end from the records observable then, on the `tenure_expected` horizon at a discount rate of 0.1. This row grades the atom it is keyed to, which it did NOT before 2026-08-25: pass 17 measured that deleting EP1's entire published output left the headline bit-identical. The belief taken is the EARLIEST year-end snapshot, which is also the only one a ceased account has -- EP1 blanks the forward horizons once an account stops settling, so a terminal table alone would grade an empty population. TRUTH-WINDOW BIAS: the realised total spans the whole lifetime while the belief is taken at the first snapshot, so truth is measured over a longer window than the belief forecasts, which flatters an over-estimating belief. SURVIVORSHIP: the graded population is every account whose life ENDED inside the run and no other, so it is selected on the quantity being predicted, and the no-skill divisor is fitted on that same selected population. A calibrated estimator scores as a uniform over-estimate here; read `components.population_selection` for the size of the shift and `components.hazard_calibration` for which way the lifetime term is actually wrong, before attributing the headline to the estimator. R12: diagnostic, never a target.

pairs.world_name: Deliverable 3: growth from the opening book is GRADUAL AND EARNED -- won and lost against the market through the acquisition physics already built, never incremented. EXIT: (a) the mechanisms named and wired, not gestured at: churn, acquisition cost, and the competitor field (W2_3_competitor_field and B4_competitor_field are the existing world/company organs; B10_competitor_switching_response is the switching response) -- this atom is the loop that makes book size THEIR outcome; (b) the falsifier IS the exit test, because the ruling states the property directly -- a growth curve that cannot be lost is not a growth curve. AMENDED 2026-08-15 (DISCOVER, worker tick) because the original wording was vacuous: it asked only that a world configuration in which the book SHRINKS be demonstrated, and at HEAD the book can ONLY shrink -- acquisition is replacement-only and can fail, so book size is monotonically non-increasing -- which means that test passes on unbuilt code, an R15 fail-open. BOTH legs are now required, from the SAME mechanism and neither bolted on: a world configuration in which the book GROWS and one in which it SHRINKS, each demonstrated, not argued; RE-AMENDED 2026-08-18 (DISCOVER, worker tick) because that wording was fail-open in the direction it ADDED: at HEAD the book already both grows (curriculum arrivals -- five staggered static I&C dates 2017-2020 plus the activated SYN-* Poisson trickle) and shrinks (churn), so it passes on unbuilt code, the identical R15 fail-open one direction over. The DIRECTION OF THE CURVE is not the test; the IDENTITY OF THE MECHANISM is -- "won and lost against the market" is not satisfied by a book that goes up and down, only by a book whose up and whose down are the SAME contest. Both legs must therefore come from the same contested mechanism, proven by a NULL CONTROL: (b1) with the arrival stream held FIXED, a change to the company's own market position alone must move book size in BOTH directions; and (b2) with the arrival stream EMPTIED, the book must still be able to grow. Truth = the term boundary the home-move win actually landed on (world answer key); the company's LIVE belief reads the predecessor's genesis anchor out of `acquisition_date`, so every re-contracted account reads as though the relationship never restarted. The headline gap is that LIVE belief -- the mechanism that fixes it (C_supply_start_semantic_separation) is BUILT but not yet ROUTED to the 7 live consumers (C_supply_start_consumer_routing), so the published tenure, cohort and 'Customer since' figures still carry the phantom. `separated_*` is the counterfactual once routed; the regime sweep shows where the world still defeats the built mechanism -- losing the activation event costs COVERAGE (honest UNKNOWN), but losing the `successor_of` link as well makes it CONFIDENTLY WRONG again, because the no-successor rung hands back the anchor. DEFENCE IN DEPTH: `*_caught_by_guard` is how many of those phantoms this atom's R10 class guard (SUPPLY_START_NOT_BEFORE_FIRST_OBSERVABLE) rejects anyway, from the account's own meter reads and bills -- observables that cannot go missing the way the registration paperwork can.

principles.title: Pursuit must be earned by confidence
principles.number: R = 8:1  →  pursue an arrears account only above ~89% confidence
principles.claim: The director signed the harm:loss weighting at R = 8:1 (harm from wrongly chasing someone who genuinely can't pay, over loss from going soft on a strategic won't-payer). Under that ratio the cost-optimal collections policy is to PURSUE an account only when the classifier is more than R/(R+1) ~ 89% confident it is a strategic non-payer — otherwise FORBEAR. At even odds (a coin-flip account) the flip-point is 1:1, so above ANY harm-aversion the ambiguous account is forborne.
principles.why: Regulation implicitly demands exactly this — pursuit is never the default, it is earned by confidence — yet no supplier can articulate the bar. We put a number on it.
principles.basis: curriculum constant (director-signed, versioned) — not a run output

principles.title: Survival is an earned result, not an assumption
principles.number: around 30 UK suppliers failed in 2021-22 — this one did not
principles.claim: Insolvency and licence revocation are terminal states in the simulation, not exceptions designed away. Around 30 real UK suppliers exited the market in the 2021-22 gas crisis; run through the same real price history under the same rules, this company survived. That makes the crisis-survival evidence an earned outcome under the worst market on record, not a modelling assumption baked in from the start.
principles.why: Anyone can model a company that cannot die. A company that CAN die, run through the worst real market on record and left standing, is the only kind whose resilience claim means anything — the point the pitch's 'why believe any of it' rests on.
principles.basis: hedged external count ('around 30') — no anchored exact figure in ASSUMPTIONS.md; the survival itself is a run outcome under the real 2021-22 price path, not an input

not_proven.claim: Why households leave this supplier, as a single share per reason
not_proven.status: measured on the renewal route only — its split is not identified, and a departure cause it cannot see is missing
not_proven.note: Every departure in this world carries the risk that fired. How those departures SPLIT between the two price reasons is not identified by any published evidence: no domestic instrument separates “my own bill rose” from “someone else is cheaper” — Ofgem's Consumer Impacts survey codes both as one answer. So the mix is published as the range it takes across every value that evidence cannot rule out: bill shock 64%–100%, our price position 0%–18%, service 0%–18%, over 148 renewals. The world itself runs at one point in that range (64% / 18% / 18%), declared as a modelling choice and argued on fidelity — it is the only end of the range where a supplier's price and service actually cause departures. The published mover-mix is deliberately NOT used to pick the point; it is reserved as a check on this output, and identifying from it would make that check a tautology. AND IT IS NOT EVERY REASON. This is a decomposition of the RENEWAL hazard, and there are causes it structurally cannot see — svt_inertia, drifting off the standard variable product — whose share is UNKNOWN here and not zero: that household strikes no rate and reaches no renewal decision, so no renewal row can carry it. On the capture behind this interval it was 49 of 84 departures, so the ranges above describe the 42% of departures this measurement can reach.

not_proven.note: That value keeps rising past broad groups into the fine-grained combinations most companies never reach is the load-bearing commercial claim; currently a hypothesis with a designed test.

deployment.what_the_two_ages_mean: RUNNING AGE is how long the process has been up; LOADED-CODE AGE is how old the code it holds is, from the commit it booted at. They answer different questions -- a daemon restarted an hour ago onto a stale checkout has a small running age and a large loaded-code age, and only the pair can say so. MODULES BEHIND stays the verdict: a daemon days behind in time that holds nothing which changed is current.
